title: Community Repair Cafe
seed_statement: We run a small community repair cafe where volunteers fix people's broken household items on Saturdays, but we keep losing track of what came in and who is working on it.

ground_truth.agency: Ana is the coordinator who logs items. Fixers work on items. Visitors just want status. Fixers only show up occasionally.
ground_truth.preconditions: Items must not collect more than a first name and phone number. Electrical items strictly require a safety test signed off by a qualified fixer before return (insurance requirement).
ground_truth.exceptions: If parts are needed, items wait. If a part never arrives after two weekends, visitor is notified and offered the item back. Unclaimed items after six weeks are decided case by case by Ana.
ground_truth.cadence: Saturday mornings. Logging an item must take under one minute to avoid queue drop-offs.
ground_truth.accountability: Every item must have an assigned fixer, an owner, and a status. Electrical safety sign-off must be recorded even if original fixer is absent.

scripted_responses: Mostly the volunteer coordinator, Ana, and the fixers themselves. Visitors just want to know when their toaster or bike is ready.
Paper tickets get lost. Some items wait three weeks because nobody remembers they need a spare part ordered.
We must not collect more personal data than a first name and a phone number. Some visitors are wary of giving anything at all.
Success would be every item having an owner and a status, and no item waiting more than two weekends without someone knowing why.
Electrical items need a qualified fixer to sign off a safety test before they go back. That is non-negotiable for our insurance.
Fixers come and go; a third of them only show up once a month, so anything they need to learn has to be obvious on the day.
We open at ten and the queue is worst in the first hour. Logging an item cannot take longer than a minute or people walk off.
